title: Habit Stacking
hook: New habits fail because they're floating around on their own. Tie them to something you already do.
statement: Attach new habits to ones you already have.
explainer: Your existing routines already run on autopilot. Hooking a new habit right after one lets it borrow that momentum instead of relying on memory or motivation.
sop: List 3 habits you do without needing motivation, like making coffee.
Score each one's Anchor strength 1 to 10.
Attach one specific new habit right after your strongest anchor.
Score the Attachment 1 to 10, how tightly it follows the anchor.
Repeat the pair daily for 2 weeks before stacking another.
equation_example: Anchor 9, a habit you never skip. Attachment 6, how tightly the new one follows. 9 × 6 = 54 out of 100. Higher means the new habit rides the old one's momentum. Lower means it's floating free and will get skipped.
question: Pick one thing you do every morning and attach one new habit right after it, starting tomorrow.
closing_statement: New habits borrow strength from old ones.
caption:
Principle Nº 137: Habit Stacking

New habits fail because they're floating around on their own. Tie them to something you already do.

Attach new habits to ones you already have.

Your turn: Pick one thing you do every morning and attach one new habit right after it, starting tomorrow.
